summary:
Forge can now use an API key from any supported LLM provider. `data/ai` has a provider registry transcribed from providers.json plus Anthropic: key patterns with confidence, base URLs and paths, JSON mode, image style, data policy, and economy/balanced/max models per job with prices and the gemini-4-carbon price change on 2026-12-01. `KeyDetector` identifies keys by shape and checks the most specific prefixes before plain sk- (OpenRouter and Anthropic first, OpenAI admin keys rejected). It rates DeepSeek sk-hex and Gemini AQ. keys as low confidence and calls sk- collisions ambiguous. When it isn't sure, saving checks the key against each candidate's GET /models (no tokens spent), and the user can always pick the provider by hand.

`AnthropicProvider` follows the Messages API rules you gave:
- version 2026-10-21, with effort always set explicitly in output_config
- no thinking, temperature, top_p or top_k fields
- JSON through output_config.format json_schema, with images placed before the text
- for Opus and Sonnet 5.5 only: fallbacks "default" and the server-side-fallback beta header
- a friendly AiException when the final stop reason is a refusal
- prompt caching on the coach's system block and last history turn
- SSE text_delta streaming, mapped errors with retries, and GET /v1/models

One `OpenAiCompatProvider` class covers OpenAI, Gemini's compat endpoint, OpenRouter, Groq, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Together and Custom. It sends images as data URIs (Mistral gets the plain-string form), asks for json_schema with strict only where it is documented, and falls back to json_object for DeepSeek. If a provider rejects optional parameters, it retries without them and finally with the schema plus an example in the prompt. It reads SSE choices[0].delta.content, skipping keep-alives and handling OpenRouter errors that arrive inside a 200.

`AiEngine` holds the provider-neutral jobs, moved out of AnthropicClient into `AiPrompts`: the upward-biased food estimate, label transcription, program parsing and coach streaming. Schemas use sentinel values instead of nullable types, `JsonExtract` recovers JSON from prose or code fences with one retry, and `AiParsers` reads fields tolerantly. `MultiProviderAi` routes each task through `ModelRouter`: per-task or DEFAULT overrides (scoped to their provider), then the tier map. Labels and the key test always use the economy model. Photo jobs fall back to a vision model, or throw a clear error, and per-model image limits are enforced.

The API key is stored in `SecretStore`: an AES-256-GCM key held in the Android Keystore, with the encrypted values in their own DataStore file that is excluded from backup. `AiKeys.migrateLegacy` moves the old plaintext key into it, blanks the plaintext, sets aiConfigured, and repairs the flag after a restore from backup.

`AiSettingsScreen` and its view model use Material 3 Expressive components. The key field shows a live detection chip and a provider picker, with save (probing if needed, then an automatic test), test and remove (with a confirmation dialog). It shows each provider's data-use note and warns when a free tier trains on your data (Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter). The tier selector shows each tier's monthly estimate, which model each job uses and its price. An Advanced section has a searchable live model list per job and a base-URL override. Loading, empty and error states and haptics are in place.

Unit tests cover key detection, JSON extraction, routing, cost and URL handling. The legacy `AnthropicClient` shim keeps ForgeRepository and OpenFoodFactsClient compiling until requests #1 to #3 are applied.

summary:
Built the guardrails, knowledge base, volume insights and coach for Forge v2, using only the verified research files. None of it has been compiled or run yet.

Guardrails.kt keeps every contract signature and implements the rules in guardrails.final.json, including the reconciliation changes:
- Calories: sex floors 1500/1200 and never below 800. Loss rate capped by body-fat tier (1.0/0.7/0.5 %BW per week). Low-confidence body-fat values are judged on their lower bound (photo -6, BIA -5, DXA 0; a null method means the caller already passes the cautious value). Deficit capped at the smaller of 25% of maintenance and 500 kcal/day.
- Gaining: monthly rate caps by training stage from the Pyramid ranges, and a surplus band from Iraki 2019.
- Macros: protein 1.6-2.2 g/kg at maintenance or above, 1.8-2.7 g/kg in a deficit (3.2 only when lean), 3.5 g/kg maximum, and 0.8 g/kg with kidney disease. Fat at least 0.5 g/kg and 20% of calories (15% in a deficit). Soft carbohydrate floors. Fibre 25 g.
- Phases and screening: diet breaks and the 16-week cut limit. Locks for minors, pregnancy (maintenance only, the 9 ACOG warning signs) and breastfeeding (+330-400 kcal). BMI under 18.5 and very low body fat block a deficit. SCOFF is asked verbatim. Energy availability and low-intake check-ins exist as helpers.
- Safety and crisis: crisis resources and a crisis phrase screen. Medical red-flag and pain stop/refer detection, safe-messaging term replacement, and a ban on water-cutting advice.
- Training and photos: fractional hard-set counting within 0-4 RIR. Volume bands of 4 / 10-20 / over 20 / over 30, frequency and per-week increase rules, RIR targets, rest, rep range and deload triggers. Load jumps over 10% return BLOCK so the program engine holds the load. Photo body fat is only ever a ±6-point range, with blocked groups.
- promptRules(profile) gives every AI prompt compact general and personal rules. Each flag carries the research's user message and citation.

NutritionMath keeps its public API. targets() now goes through checkNutrition, and a new checkedTargets() also returns the flags that explain any change. The gain default is the midpoint of the training-stage band. goalFeedback no longer praises fast drops and frames changes as at most 10% after two weeks.

KnowledgeBase is rewritten from the research (about 4k tokens). It covers training (including Pelland, Schoenfeld 2017, Baz-Valle, Robinson/Refalo, rest, progression, deloads, and lengthened partials described as emerging), nutrition (including Morton 2018, the deficit protein ranges, Garthe, Murphy & Koehler, diet breaks), recovery and wearables, supplements, and a source-trust order built on the GVS 2025 tier list.

VolumeAnalyzer counts weekly hard sets per muscle on a rolling 7-day window against the previous 7 days. Primary muscles count 1, secondary 0.5. Exercises are matched by catalog id, then by name; unmatched ones are skipped and listed. Sets logged with more than 4 RIR (or RPE below 6) are excluded. The catalog lookup is injectable, so it runs in JVM tests.

TrainingVolumeSection draws animated bars per muscle against the evidence bands, with the guardrail flags and real loading, empty and error states.

Coach:
- The system prompt is persona + evidence base + source trust + promptRules + a rich data block: profile and health answers, active plan and check-in, targets, the last 14 days of intake, the 7-day average weight and trend, the program, best sets, weekly volume per muscle, and wearable data against the person's own baseline.
- detectCrisis runs on every message before the model sees it. If it matches, a crisis card with tap-to-dial buttons appears immediately, the plan feature's 30-day lock is recorded, and the model still answers supportively but gives no advice that turn. Medical and pain messages get their own safety cards.
- Also included: four quick-prompt chips, light Markdown in bubbles, smooth frame-paced typing of the stream, the answering model shown in the header and under replies, and clear chat with a confirmation.

There are JVM tests for both Guardrails and VolumeAnalyzer. The only request filed is optional (a settings key for the large-deficit opt-in).

The unit of WHOOP's X-RateLimit-Reset header isn't in the research. The code treats it as seconds and caps the wait at 120 s (60 s if unreadable).

WHOOP body_measurement isn't imported. The scope is still requested per the research, but the weight is a profile value, not a weigh-in. WHOOP's absolute skin temperature is kept only in the WHOOP layer, never in skinTempDeltaC, which holds a deviation.

The research has no Android package ids for Google Health/Fitbit, Oura or COROS. They are recognised by matching the installed app's label (display only). Data relayed through Health Sync can't be credited to Huawei.

Readiness uses mean ±1 SD of the person's own history as 'usual'. This is a statistical choice made for the app, not a threshold from the research, and the UI says so. Overall needs ≥2 components. Sleep only counts against when it is shorter than usual.

Health Connect sleep is now assigned to the wake date (sessions, minus awake stages) instead of the aggregate that splits a night across two days. Rows synced after this will differ from v1 rows for the same night.

Per-field provenance lives in files/wearables/{health_connect,whoop,apple}.json, because health_daily has no column for it. If those files are lost, existing row values are kept and provenance rebuilds on the next sync.

The Apple import only looks for an entry named export.xml inside the zip. Localised export names aren't handled. Workouts only count toward exercise minutes, and ActivitySummary and workout routes are ignored.

summary:
I built the Wearables area, filed one request file, and did not run Gradle, so none of this has been compiled or tested yet.

Health Connect: HealthConnectManager keeps its v1 API and now also reads RMSSD HRV, VO2 max, SpO2, respiratory rate, lean mass and skin temperature (when the phone supports it). It asks for past-data and background access when supported and tracks which app each value came from. Raw readings are reduced to one value per day from a single source, so two devices are never averaged together. Sleep counts toward the day you wake up.

Merging: each source (Health Connect, the WHOOP API, an Apple import) keeps its own per-day file, and every health_daily row is rebuilt from all of them through WearableDao. Per field, a dedicated device beats the phone; on a tie, the WHOOP API beats Health Connect, which beats an Apple import. A field no source reports keeps its old value, and Apple's SDNN never goes into the RMSSD column. The old readDailies() path also goes through this merge now, so the existing ForgeRepository.syncHealth can't overwrite WHOOP or Apple fields.

WearableSync.syncAll() matches the contract, and overlapping calls share one sync. Background sync runs every 6 hours when the battery isn't low.

WHOOP: the user registers their own Sandbox app and pastes the client ID and secret, which go into SecretStore. Sign-in uses a Custom Tab with an 8-character state that survives the app being killed, and the redirect URI is forge://whoop/callback. Token refreshes are serialized and the new token pair is saved as one value. Requests page through results and stay under the rate limit. Recovery, HRV, resting HR, SpO2, strain, calories, sleep, respiratory rate and workouts are stored exactly as WHOOP reports them.

Apple import: picks export.zip (or a bare export.xml) and streams it with XmlPullParser, with progress and cancel. Days use the time offset stored in the export. When an iPhone and a Watch both count steps, the larger source wins instead of the two being added. Weigh-ins import as APPLE_HEALTH, at most one per day and never on a day that already has one.

Readiness: compares the 7-day average of ln(RMSSD) with the 60 days before it, resting HR with the past 60 days, and last night's sleep with the past 30 nights. It shows a coarse label rather than a score, explains each component and says what data is missing. WHOOP recovery is shown as reported.

UI: the Wearables screen has a sync card, the Health Connect permission and install flow, sources seen, the WHOOP walkthrough with the redirect URI to copy, the Apple import card (which states plainly that Apple Watch can't sync to Android), and 12 brand cards with setup steps and caveats taken from the research. ReadinessCard and WearableTrendsSection (HRV, resting HR, sleep, steps, VO2 max, WHOOP recovery, Apple SDNN shown separately) replace the stubs with the same signatures.

Tests cover the readiness math, the merge rules, and Apple day aggregation from an inline export.xml sample (Robolectric, SDK 35).

summary:
I built Forge v2's design system and shell, in the PixelPlayer style. Nothing has been compiled, per the contract.

**Theme (ui/theme):**
- MaterialExpressiveTheme with hand-tuned ember light/dark schemes and AMOLED black.
- Dynamic colour is optional and wrapped in try/catch.
- MotionScheme.expressive(), or standard() when reduce motion is on.
- Rounder shapes, and Google Sans Flex typography using FontVariation with opsz/ROND per role. All 30 styles set, with tabular figures.
- ForgeTheme reads settings itself and provides LocalForgeSettings, LocalReduceMotion and haptics gated on settings.haptics.
- A stateless ForgeAppearanceTheme is used by the previews and tests.
- ForgeNavTransitions holds PixelPlayer push/pop and directional tab tweens, chosen so predictive back can scrub them.

**Components:** all existing APIs stay source-compatible, restyled to Expressive:
- Cards are 24 dp; MacroBar is drawn in the draw phase with a rolling counter.
- CalorieRing uses a spring and gains an optional centre slot.
- EmptyState has a cookie-shaped badge that pops in.

Toolkit added:
- press-scale and bounceClick modifiers with haptics
- intro stagger
- AnimatedCounter (rolling digits)
- shimmer skeletons
- ExpressiveLoading
- ForgeTopBar / ForgeSubScreen (large collapsing top bar)
- SwipeToDeleteRow (the PixelPlayer tension gesture) with a showUndo snackbar helper
- segmented list rows, ConnectedChoiceGroup and IconBadge
- FloatingNavBar, whose single indicator stretches with velocity, and a cookie-shaped ExpressiveFab

**Shell (MainActivity):**
- core-splashscreen, held until settings load, with an animated flame icon and an animator exit.
- Edge-to-edge with transparent bars.
- A floating pill bar plus a log-food FAB for top-level routes. It hides via a graphicsLayer translation on detail routes and when the IME is open.
- One app-wide snackbar.
- Still calls ForgeNavHost(nav, modifier) and uses Routes.

**Screens:**
- **Today:** pull-to-refresh via WearableSync, an animated day header, a hero ring with counters and 2x2 macro bars, the plan and readiness slots, weight and steps tiles, quick-add with undo, and a meal timeline with swipe-to-delete and undo. It has loading, error and empty states, respects hideNumbers, and uses PlanTargets first.
- **Trends:** the existing charts, with series precomputed in the view model, plus the training and wearable slots.
- **Log:** every existing flow kept, plus a direct Label mode, morphing stage transitions, provider-neutral copy and safe saves.
- **Settings:** a grouped hub with inline food-logging options and About/licences.
- **Appearance:** live theme thumbnails and switches.

**Also:**
- New adaptive launcher icon (gradient flame foreground, glow background, even-odd monochrome).
- Roborazzi test rendering Today in light and dark.
- Request file docs/contracts/requests/design-shell.md, with the ForgeNavHost transition snippet and the onOpenWearables wiring.

RPE table: derived from Epley/Brzycki using RIR = 10 - RPE (the Zourdos RIR-based scale cited in feature_ideas.json). No third-party RPE percentage chart is used.

Reminders are WorkManager one-time jobs that reschedule themselves, so Doze can deliver them a few minutes late (the UI says so). A job more than 3 hours late is skipped. The weigh-in reminder is suppressed while edScreenPositive is set (conservative reading of the guardrail locks). The Today widget hides all numbers when hideNumbers or edScreenPositive is on.

Widgets use GlanceTheme defaults (system dynamic colours on Android 12+), not Forge's private brand ColorScheme. There is no preview image or layout. The widget-info XMLs have no description until the strings request lands.

Backup JSON does not include settings/profile, API keys, the barcode cache, or meal and progress photo files. Restoring settings would need SettingsStore setters and was left out on purpose. Restore matches existing programs by name+createdAt, and maps days of an existing program by orderIdx.

Exercise linking on import depends on ExerciseCatalog.resolve (owned by Exercises). Imported SetLog.exerciseName keeps the original name and exerciseId is set when a candidate resolves. The candidates tried are the raw name, 'Equipment Base' (e.g. 'Barbell Bench Press'), and the bare movement.

summary:
Built the full Tools, widgets, data and reminders area against CONTRACTS.md, touching only files this area owns.

Tools (feature/tools): ToolsScreen has four tabs, switched with connected ToggleButtons.
- Plates: a target-weight field with stepper buttons, an animated plate-stack Canvas per side using theme colours, grouped plate pills, and the nearest lower/higher load. A gym-profile editor covers bar 20/15/10 kg, collars on/off with weight, and a count per side for each plate from 25 down to 0.5 kg. The profile is stored in its own DataStore file.
- Warm-up: starts from the empty bar at 2x5, then even jumps to the work weight (per the verified Starting Strength guidance). Reps taper, and every load is rounded to what the plates can build.
- 1RM: Epley and Brzycki estimates with RPE folded in as reps in reserve, a 50-100% table where tapping a row loads that weight on the Plates tab, and a derived RPE grid.
- Convert: kg/lb, cm/in and kcal/kJ.
The pure helpers (PlateMath, WarmupGenerator, OneRepMax, Units) are public so other features can call them. PlateMath solves plate combinations exactly, so limited inventories work where a biggest-plate-first approach fails.

Widgets (feature/widgets, Glance): 'Today' shows a calorie ring (bitmap arcs tinted with GlanceTheme colours), protein as a bar, and a Log food deep link. It switches between small and wide layouts and shows no numbers when hideNumbers or a positive eating-disorder screen is set. 'Next workout' rotates through the active program's days, shows a session in progress, and lists the first exercises at taller sizes. ForgeWidgets provides updateAll, requestUpdate and a debounced auto-refresh from Room and settings flows. The widget-info XMLs refresh every 30 minutes.

Reminders (data/reminders): one-time WorkManager jobs for weigh-in, the evening food check (fires only if fewer than 2 entries are logged) and training days (user-chosen weekdays, skipped if a session is already logged), each rescheduling itself. They are controlled by the settings toggles. Times and training days live in their own DataStore file. Notifications go to a 'forge_reminders' channel, open the app through forge:// deep links, and use neutral copy that follows the guardrails.

Data (data/backup + DataSettingsScreen):
- Export: one JSON backup (versioned format, every field defaulted) and four CSVs (food, weights, workouts/sets, measurements) via SAF CreateDocument. The CSVs use locale-safe numbers, a BOM, and protection against spreadsheet formula injection.
- Restore: a Forge backup is merged in one transaction, deduplicated on natural keys, with foreign-key remapping and a confirmation preview first.
- Hevy/Strong import: CSV workout history is imported with a preview showing duplicates, linked and unlinked exercises, and a kg/lb choice for files that don't name a unit.
- Reminders section: toggles, time pickers, training-day chips, and the POST_NOTIFICATIONS request with a link to system settings.
- Storage: a breakdown of what Forge stores, plus 'delete meal photos' behind a confirmation.

BackupDao was extended. The integration requests are filed in docs/contracts/requests/tools-widgets-data.md: manifest receivers, widget strings, two start() calls in ForgeApp, and navDeepLinks in ForgeNavHost. JVM tests were added for PlateMath, warm-ups, 1RM, the Hevy/Strong parsers, CSV handling, the next-workout picker and reminder time maths. Gradle was not run, so none of this has been compiled yet.
